newsitem.title: UGANDA: Tanzania, Uganda airlines in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania, Uganda airlines in merger talks.

text.p: The governments of Tanzania and Uganda are in talks to merge their national airlines with Alliance Air, in which they are already partners with South African Airways (SAA), Alliance said on Tuesday.
Alliance company secretary Fred Obbo told Reuters from the firm's head office in the Ugandan capital, Kampala, that the national airlines would cease to exist as separate entities.
"We will just have one airline," Obbo said.
Air Tanzania and Uganda Airlines have since the start-up of Alliance in 1995 been limited to flying routes within Africa.

In Kampala, the board of Uganda Airlines was meeting on the merger plans on Tuesday. In Dar es Salaam, Air Tanzania executives and government officials were also thrashing out details of the merger on Tuesday.
Both airlines said they would not immediately discuss any matters related to the merger. Previously, each country had put emphasis on privatising its national airline.
Asked if they would continue to operate as separate airlines, Obbo said: "No, not at all."
The two countries each own a 30 percent stake in Alliance, with SAA, South Africa's national carrier, owning 40 percent.
SAA provides technical services to the airline which flies twice a week to London and between Dar es Salaam, Entebbe and Johannesburg.

Fanie Brandt, Alliance's marketing manager in Kampala told Reuters the ministers of transport of Uganda and Tanzania met on February 17 to discuss several issues, including the merger of the three carriers. The matter would have to be put to the respective national cabinets.
"Then consultants will be appointed to evaluate the modalities involved and their report has to be in by the end of June," Brandt said.
The merger was intended to cut costs.
"At the moment we have three different companies often serving the same route. It will make it more economically viable to have one company," he said.
Neither Obbo nor Brandt could provide details of the intended shareholdings of the merged company.
"The political decision has been made. How that is done and what the share structures will be, I do not know but I imagine there will be some changes in structure," Obbo said.
He added that no decision had been taken on a name for the new airline but that this was likely to be settled by the end of June. Routes also still needed to be agreed.
